research_problem: REST test generators' oracles only catch crashes, spec violations, regressions and best-practice violations; spec-conformant but wrong responses go undetected
technical_approach: AGORA: Beet instrumenter maps OAS + request/response logs to Daikon traces (with nested levels for arrays of objects); customized Daikon with 105 REST invariant types (22 new); likely invariants become oracles after confirmation
primary_contribution: First likely-invariant-based black-box test oracle generation for REST APIs
dataset_benchmark: 11 operations of 7 industrial APIs (Amadeus, GitHub, Marvel, OMDb, Spotify, Yelp, YouTube); 10K RESTest calls per operation
evaluation_metrics: Precision of invariants (manual TP/FP labeling); failure detection ratio on 1.1M response-level seeded errors
key_findings: Precision 81.2% vs Daikon 51.4% (93.6% excluding arithmetic comparisons); 50 requests already give 73.2%; oracles detect 57.3% of seeded output errors; 11 real bugs (4 confirmed, 2 fixed) and a GitHub documentation update
author_limitations: Manually created/fixed specs; manual input dictionaries; human labeling bias; single random split; 11 operations; incomplete invariant catalogue; operation-level only, JSON only
analyst_limitations: Mutation operators mirror invariant types (favourable FDR); real-fault recall unknown; manual FP review cost; weak baseline; inputs from same-group RESTest; stateful/write APIs untested
reproducibility: Zenodo artifact with code, data and VM; Beet open-source; live APIs drift
suggested_extensions: Sequence-level invariants; LLM-assisted invariant triage/explanation; evaluation on real-fault benchmarks; write invariants back into specs; combine with online testing
evidence_location: Approach p.4-6; RQs p.6-7; Table 2 p.9; RQ3 p.9 Table 3; bugs p.9-10; threats p.10
integrity: Table 2 column-split but totals reconstructable; sunburst figure partial
